item.title: Lion tracks from the ice age: How two ways of seeing brought ancient animals to life
item.description: The coastline near the southern tip of Africa looked vastly different between about 400,000 years ago and 70,000 years ago, compared with today. At times it lay as much as 100km (62 miles) south of its present location, exposing the vast Palaeo-Agulhas Plain, which contained an extensive habitat for large mammals. At other times the sea level was briefly as much as 13 meters (43 feet) higher than today's mean level. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Solving the mystery behind a flightless beetle's transatlantic journey
item.description: They can't fly or swim, so why do their closest relatives appear on different continents? What's more, North America's largest tiger beetles are related to these ancestral South American giant tiger beetles. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Scorecard: Colombia gets top marks while high-emitting countries doing too little to protect health from climate change
item.description: The latest Healthy NDC Scorecard, published by the Global Climate and Health Alliance, finds that, Colombia integrates health most deeply into its national climate plan, closely followed by Nigeria and Cambodia. item.title: Alguien ha robado 100 millones de dólares en criptomonedas utilizando puertas traseras plantadas de antemano en monederos físicos
item.description: Cuando hablamos de proteger nuestras criptomonedas, solemos pensar en contraseñas, estafas por Internet o ataques informáticos. Sin embargo, existe otra dimensión de la seguridad que puede pasar más inadvertida: la integridad del dispositivo físico al que confiamos las claves de acceso a nuestros fondos. Podemos comprar un monedero auténtico, recibirlo en su embalaje y comprobar que funciona aparentemente con normalidad. Pero ninguna de esas circunstancias garantiza por sí sola que nadie haya manipulado su interior. Y ese es precisamente el tipo de riesgo que puede poner en cuestión incluso… Fuente: Xataka.

item.title: Zimbabwean author Simbarashe Kundizeza denies using AI to write prize-winning story
item.description: Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated. Kundizeza’s story The Blue Fighter was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later, The Atlantic published an article by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.”… Fuente: The Guardian - World.
